gap: No result ChatGPT got says how long either kit's indoor screen works away from a wall outlet. eufy's Smart Display E10 is rated for over 6 hours of live streaming, and eufy stops battery-camera live view after 3 minutes, so one charge covers about 120 full doorbell live views (6 h × 60 ÷ 3 min). SwitchBot's monitor has no battery and runs only on AC mains (0 views unplugged).
standout_why: I checked three pages. The cited smarthomeperfected.com page lists the SwitchBot monitor as 'Needs a power cable' but gives no runtime, price or battery figures for the eufy E10 or the E340 doorbell. Its only derived number is about 20 mAh per day for the TKMARS kit. worthrated.com (top result in chat 2) covers only wired LUMOBELL, TMEZON and AMOCAM intercoms and gives no prices, runtimes or per-unit figures. eufy's own bundle page (cited) shows the 4,050 mAh battery and an 'All-Day Power' heading but does not state the runtime or the 3-minute live-view limit. None of the three gives a doorbell's mAh per day or says whether the bundle actually saves money.
decides: This is the split between ChatGPT's two catalog cards. If the shopper wants to carry the screen around the house, only the eufy E10 can do it, and it lasts about one day off the dock (over 24 h with the screen off, about 120 live views of 3 minutes). The SwitchBot monitor has to stay plugged in. Both doorbells use about the same battery per day (around 36 mAh), so doorbell battery life does not separate them. Price does: SwitchBot is $149.99 against $419.99 for eufy. Also, eufy's $419.99 bundle costs 1 cent more than buying the E10 ($249.99) and E340 ($169.99) separately ($419.98), so the 'bundle' saves nothing today. ChatGPT showed the bundle at $399.98.
